title: Relative timestamps — write a helper, or take the dependency?
notes: Tests the agent's own stated rule against itself. Its evaluation reference says to try writing it yourself first, but explicitly carves out dates as a category where the naive implementation is wrong in ways you will not discover for a year. The correct answer is neither reflex: Intl.RelativeTimeFormat and Intl.DateTimeFormat are platform APIs that cover both requirements with no dependency at all, which beats both moment.js and a hand-rolled helper. moment.js specifically is in maintenance mode and large. The failure mode being tested is applying the 'just write it' heuristic to a timezone- and locale-sensitive problem, or recommending a library without checking core first.

expect.name: points at the built-in Intl APIs rather than a library or a hand-rolled helper
flags moment.js as the wrong choice for a new codebase
treats locale-aware absolute dates as the harder half of the requirement
does not recommend hand-rolling date logic

forbid.name: recommends writing a custom relative-time helper from scratch
invents a bundle size number for moment
